components.css: :root{--ink:#0a0d12;--mint:#cce3ff;--pale:#f3f6fa;--bone:#ece9e2;--coral:#f4a18b;--amber:#ffcc5c;--text:#eceff4;--mute:#a4adbb;--line:rgba(230,236,245,.12);--ease-out:cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1);--spring:cubic-bezier(.34,1.36,.5,1);--sans:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'SF Pro Text','Nunito Sans',system-ui,sans-serif;--display:'Nunito',ui-rounded,'SF Pro Rounded',system-ui,sans-serif;--mono:'JetBrains Mono',ui-monospace,'SF Mono',monospace;}.ds-btn-primary{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:10px;height:54px;padding:0 24px;border-radius:14px;font:650 1.02rem/1 var(--sans);letter-spacing:-.005em;text-decoration:none;background:var(--pale);color:var(--ink);box-shadow:0 10px 24px -12px rgba(0,0,0,.7);transition:transform .25s var(--ease-out),box-shadow .25s,background .2s}.ds-btn-primary:hover{background:#fff;transform:translateY(-1px);box-shadow:0 16px 30px -14px rgba(0,0,0,.8)}.ds-btn-primary:active{transform:translateY(0)}.ds-btn-primary:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:3px}

components.css: :root{--ink:#0a0d12;--mint:#cce3ff;--pale:#f3f6fa;--bone:#ece9e2;--coral:#f4a18b;--amber:#ffcc5c;--text:#eceff4;--mute:#a4adbb;--line:rgba(230,236,245,.12);--ease-out:cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1);--spring:cubic-bezier(.34,1.36,.5,1);--sans:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'SF Pro Text','Nunito Sans',system-ui,sans-serif;--display:'Nunito',ui-rounded,'SF Pro Rounded',system-ui,sans-serif;--mono:'JetBrains Mono',ui-monospace,'SF Mono',monospace;}.ds-notch{position:relative;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;width:196px;height:32px;padding:0 12px 0 10px;background:#000;color:#fff;border-radius:0 0 14px 14px;margin:0 auto;transition:width .5s var(--spring)}.ds-notch:hover{width:236px}.ds-notch::before,.ds-notch::after{content:'';position:absolute;top:0;width:10px;height:10px}.ds-notch::before{left:-10px;background:radial-gradient(circle at 0 100%,transparent 9.5px,#000 10px)}.ds-notch::after{right:-10px;background:radial-gradient(circle at 100% 100%,transparent 9.5px,#000 10px)}.ds-drop{width:14px;height:18px;background:var(--mint);border-radius:50% 50% 50% 50%/60% 60% 40% 40%}.ds-brand{font:800 13px/1 var(--display);color:rgba(255,255,255,.86)}

components.name: Pulled Sheet
components.description: An ebru sheet with a bone held edge, slightly rotated; straightens on hover. Carries a feature's real UI.
components.css: :root{--ink:#0a0d12;--mint:#cce3ff;--pale:#f3f6fa;--bone:#ece9e2;--coral:#f4a18b;--amber:#ffcc5c;--text:#eceff4;--mute:#a4adbb;--line:rgba(230,236,245,.12);--ease-out:cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1);--spring:cubic-bezier(.34,1.36,.5,1);--sans:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'SF Pro Text','Nunito Sans',system-ui,sans-serif;--display:'Nunito',ui-rounded,'SF Pro Rounded',system-ui,sans-serif;--mono:'JetBrains Mono',ui-monospace,'SF Mono',monospace;}.ds-sheet{margin:0;max-width:320px;font-family:var(--sans);color:var(--text)}.ds-paper{aspect-ratio:4/3;border-radius:2px;background:radial-gradient(circle at 30% 40%,#cce3ff 0 10%,#3a5a8a 10% 16%,transparent 16%),radial-gradient(circle at 70% 60%,#ece9e2 0 8%,#8fb3e6 8% 13%,transparent 13%),#162236;box-shadow:0 0 0 9px var(--bone),0 34px 50px -30px rgba(0,0,0,.95);transform:rotate(-1.2deg);transition:transform .6s var(--ease-out)}.ds-sheet:hover .ds-paper{transform:rotate(0) translateY(-4px)}.ds-sheet figcaption{margin-top:28px;display:grid;gap:8px}.ds-sheet b{font:850 1.35rem/1.15 var(--display);letter-spacing:-.015em}.ds-sheet span{color:var(--mute);font-size:.98rem}.ds-sheet small{font-size:.8rem;font-style:italic;color:#737e8f}

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Ebru Tray"**

Damla means drop, and the site is a tray of dark water. The ground is near-black cool ink, the same black as the notch it hangs from. Pigment lands on it only in two ways: once, when the page opens and a drop falls from the notch and is pulled into a tulip, and afterwards only when the visitor clicks. A drag combs what is there, and scrolling pulls slow tines through it. Everything else holds still. Calm water is the default state, and pigment is an event.

The pigments are Damla's own in-app colours, not a generic marbling palette. The agents' pale water blue leads, white is the default accent, bone is the paper, and the demo cover's coral is used sparingly. Amber means one thing, as it does in the app: something is waiting. The product appears as a faithful replica of the live panel, drawn at the app's native point size in the system font and scaled as one piece, so the page shows the real thing rather than an illustration of it.

The page reads as a sequence: the tray, a pinned stage where the panel melts out of the notch and turns its pages, a book of pulled ebru sheets for the smaller features, a quiet privacy statement, and a finale where the visitor's own marbling is pulled as a print. Liquid Glass lens effects were tried on this surface and rejected; so were automatic pours, a mint accent, and "demo data" disclaimers.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black cool ink ground; calm until the visitor touches it.
Tonal blue pigments with bone paper and a sparing coral.
Rounded heavy display (Nunito 850–900) over the Mac's own system text.
The product appears as an exact-scale replica of the live panel, never a mockup.
Pulled paper sheets with bone edges, slightly rotated, carry secondary features.
The site nav is a black notch at the top centre.

rules.name: The Own Colours Rule
rules.body: Every accent on the page is a colour the app itself uses. Water blue, white, coral from the cover, amber for waiting. Nothing is imported from a generic marbling or SaaS palette, and there is no mint.

rules.name: The Amber Means Waiting Rule
rules.body: Amber is never decorative. If it is on screen, something is waiting for the user.

rules.name: The Calm Water Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds stay calm. The ground is dark tonal blues combed into slow ribbons; bright pigment covers a small share of any viewport and arrives only from the opening drop or a visitor's click.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Commands Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only where the visitor would type or copy something. It is never a stylistic label face.

rules.name: The Replica Follows The App Rule
rules.body: Inside the panel replica and the sheet vignettes, type is the Mac system font at the app's own point sizes (for example 16.5px track titles, 12.5px buttons). The replica never adopts the site's display or body scale.

rules.name: The No Lens Rule
rules.body: No Liquid Glass lens, refraction or frosted-glass cards on the site. The only blur is a light 6px backdrop behind the command field so the command stays legible over pigment.

dos: **Do** keep the ground near-black cool ink (`ink`, `ink-2`, `ink-3`) and let pigment arrive only from the opening drop or a visitor's click; a drag combs, scrolling pulls slow tines.
**Do** lead with water blue (`water-blue`) and white (`pale-white`); keep coral to cover-tinted details and a single ring in the water.
**Do** use amber (`waiting-amber`) only for waiting state.
**Do** draw product UI at the app's native point size in the system font and scale it as one piece, matching the live app.
**Do** give every sheet a bone held edge, a slight rotation and its feature's real UI.
**Do** keep JetBrains Mono for commands and code only.
**Do** honour Reduce Motion: drops land at once, combs and loops stop, the page stays fully readable.
donts: **Don't** pour colour into the water automatically, on a timer, or on page changes.
**Don't** label the replica or its content as "demo data".
**Don't** use a Liquid Glass lens, refraction or frosted-glass cards.
**Don't** introduce a mint or teal site accent.
**Don't** make backgrounds busy: no bright full-field pigment, no constant motion behind copy.
**Don't** set the panel replica in Nunito or at the site's body sizes.
